Discovery, with Paramount potentially agreeing to preserve CNN's editorial independence and divest certain cable channels including Comedy Central. tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your Monday September 21st morning brief.

Markets are opening the week on a surprisingly strong note given how negative the weekend news flow was. S&P futures are up about 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq is up 110 basis points, and the Russell 2000 is up roughly 47 basis points. Asia closed broadly higher — Korea led with gains of 1.65%, Hong Kong added 1.18%, and mainland China was up about 1 percent. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points with strength in industrials, tech, and banks. Treasury yields are down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve, providing a mild tailwind.

The key question this morning is why stocks are rallying when almost every piece of weekend news was negative. The answer seems to be diplomatic optimism around the United Nations General Assembly in New York, which runs through September 28th. Trump has signaled openness to meeting with Iran's president who is expected to attend, and he reportedly pulled back from authorizing air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. Markets are betting that even a tiny improvement in Middle East tensions could trigger a sharp drop in oil — Brent is already sliding 170 basis points to around 102 dollars a barrel — and that would unleash a cascade of bullish macro effects including lower yields, reduced inflation, margin relief, and better consumer sentiment.

But the bear case is real and cannot be ignored. The Houthis dramatically escalated their attacks on Saudi Arabia over the weekend. Ukraine launched its largest-ever drone strike on Russia. Motor oil is being rationed at US retailers. Oil tanker costs are surging. And on the AI front, the weekend brought a wave of troubling headlines — Anthropic's IPO has been delayed, its 2027 revenue projections disappointed, OpenAI is projecting negative free cash flow of roughly 280 billion dollars over the next four years, and Oracle's data center debt tied to its New Mexico facility has, quote, hit a wall, according to the Financial Times. The broader AI off-balance-sheet liability exposure across Big Tech is up roughly 300 billion dollars in just the last twelve months.

On individual names, Novo Nordisk is sliding in Europe after failing to provide sufficiently granular financial targets at its analyst meeting today. Disney's parks business is bucking an industry-wide traffic slump by leaning into price promotions. Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery remain in regulatory limbo as Paramount negotiates a settlement with California's attorney general over their merger, with potential divestitures of cable assets including Comedy Central. Nscale, a London-based neocloud company, filed its S1 Friday and plans to list on the New York Stock Exchange.

On the Fed, both Kansas City's Schmid and Minneapolis's Kashkari spoke over the weekend and both were hawkish — warning that inflation is broad-based and not just an oil story. The market is pricing about 33 basis points of additional rate hikes over the final two Fed meetings this year.

The big catalysts this week beyond the UN General Assembly are the US flash PMIs Wednesday morning, the Trump and Xi summit Thursday, and earnings from Costco Thursday night. The directional call for today is a diplomatic-optimism-driven bid that feels fragile. Watch oil. If it keeps falling, the bulls are in charge. If it reverses, the weekend's bad news reasserts itself quickly. Stay nimble.
